text:
Garry Kasparov is a renowned Russian chess grandmaster, former world champion, and prominent political activist. He began his chess career at a young age, winning the Soviet Junior Championship at 13 and rising rapidly through the ranks, becoming world No. 1 at 22. He defeated Anatoly Karpov in 1985 to claim the world title, a victory that marked the beginning of a legendary rivalry. Kasparov held the top rating for over two decades, achieving a peak Elo rating of 2851 in 1999, and remained the world's top-ranked player until his retirement in 2005.
Beyond chess, Kasparov is known for his deep engagement in politics, particularly his opposition to Vladimir Putin's government in Russia. After leaving the Communist Party in 1990, he became a vocal critic of authoritarianism, advocating for democratic reforms and human rights. He co-founded the United Civil Front and ran as a presidential candidate in 2008, though he withdrew due to difficulties in securing meeting spaces. In 2013, he fled Russia due to political persecution, citing fear of arrest and suppression of dissent. From exile, he has continued to speak out against Russian actions, including the invasion of Ukraine, and has criticized the Kremlin's policies on human rights, freedom of speech, and the use of force.
Kasparov has also made significant contributions to chess beyond competition, including co-authoring books on opening theory and developing new variants, such as the "Kasparov Gambit." He has participated in numerous team events, winning medals in eight Chess Olympiads and representing both the Soviet Union and Russia. In the post-retirement era, he has remained active in chess through exhibitions, training young players, and promoting the game globally via initiatives like Kasparov Chess, a subscription-based online platform.
In addition to his chess and political work, Kasparov has engaged in public debates on artificial intelligence, the future of technology, and the role of human agency in a rapidly evolving world. He has also been involved in public discourse on international affairs, including the Israeli–Palestinian conflict, the use of force in foreign policy, and the need for global cooperation to counter authoritarianism. His influence extends into education, where he has advocated for the integration of chess into school curricula as a tool for developing critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
